purpose: Stress-test the Creator Corpus Census and Source Transmission architecture against a real fragmented historical corpus before freezing relational tables.
governingRules: A title attestation is not automatically a Historical Work.
Conflicting title, date, and identity claims remain separate until adjudicated.
Source-circle association never changes public authorship automatically.
Documented association may coexist with an unknown historical mechanism.
Recovery state is multidimensional and does not substitute for a full Recovery Work audit.
This packet is evidence-bearing research input, not production publication truth.

nameClaims.notes: Government copyright catalog heading; do not model Alice Mary Ross as a pseudonym merely because later aggregators do so.

creatorCorpus.reason: The publisher archive alone attests 26 later titles/projects, while surviving digitized early works and other bibliographic sources add titles outside that archive. No exhaustive authority/holdings sweep has yet established COMPLETE_AS_KNOWN.

sourceRegistry.title: Dodd, Mead mss., 1855-1992
sourceRegistry.notes: Finding aid describes the underlying primary publisher archive and lists Alice Ross Colver files, 1929-1960, for 26 title/project strings. The archive itself contains agreements, correspondence, copyright statements and related publisher records.

sourceRegistry.title: The Wish fairy and Dewy Dear
sourceRegistry.notes: LOC records Alice Ross Colver, Henry Altemus Company, 1922, LCCN 22008427, 63+[1] pages, color frontispiece/illustrations, complete PDF/text/images and public-domain reuse statement.

sourceRegistry.title: Jeanne's house party
sourceRegistry.notes: LOC records Alice Ross Colver, illustrator J. M. Clifton, Penn Publishing, 1923, LCCN 23017721, OCLC 21382185, complete PDF/text/images and public-domain reuse statement.

sourceRegistry.title: The dear pretender
sourceRegistry.notes: LOC records Alice Ross Colver, Penn Publishing, 1924, LCCN 24005100, OCLC 10445728, complete PDF/text/images and public-domain reuse statement.

sourceRegistry.title: Henry Altemus Company - Wish Fairy Series 190
sourceRegistry.notes: Lists four Wish Fairy Series title strings; states the first three were initially in Wee Books for Wee Folks, all four were catalogued in the Wish Fairy Series in 1922, and Mud Wumps has never been seen and may not have been published.

sourceRegistry.title: Henry Altemus Co - Wee Books for Wee Folks

sourceRegistry.title: Author Info
sourceRegistry.notes: Image Cascade states gratitude to authors and authors' families for permitting it to bring works back, making the currently republished Joan Foster line rights-sensitive for Write Now until independently adjudicated.

sourceRegistry.title: American Women Writers of Fiction 1910-1960 (C)
sourceRegistry.notes: Lists Alice [Mary] Ross Colver, née Ross, aka Mary Randall, and describes her Babs, Jeanne, and Joan Foster series and broader career.

sourceRegistry.title: New General Catalog of Old Books & Authors
sourceRegistry.notes: Lists Alice (Mary) née Ross Colver and explicitly cross-references pseudonym Mary Randall; also supplies early title strings, some with dates that conflict with stronger sources.

sourceRegistry.title: Alice Ross Colver
sourceRegistry.notes: Useful only as a discovery/series cross-check. It repeats Mary Randall and Alice Mary Ross as pen names, but the government copyright heading shows Alice Mary (Ross) Colver is a documented personal-name form and should not be canonicalized as a pseudonym.

sourceCircleRecords.notes: This packet deliberately does not decide whether the Mary Randall relationship is best modeled as private pseudonym, reusable byline, house identity, source circle, or another transmission mechanism.

sourceCircleMemberships.notes: Multiple secondary bibliographic sources explicitly associate Mary Randall with Alice Ross Colver. This establishes the association as documented evidence for the research graph without establishing the historical mechanism or changing Alice Ross Colver's public byline.

Exact distinctive title under same creator, with government copyright evidence and publisher archive attestation.

coverageLimitations: This is not an exhaustive corpus census and must not be labeled COMPLETE_AS_KNOWN.
No exhaustive WorldCat holdings census was performed in this packet.
No title-by-title Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks, LibriVox, Hoopla, OverDrive, Palace, or CloudLibrary recovery audit was completed here.
No full rights determination was performed for later works or current Image Cascade editions.
Dodd, Mead archive title strings are attestations, not automatic proof that each item was published as a distinct book.
Modern aggregator dates are discovery aids only where stronger evidence is absent.
Mary Randall association is documented as a bibliographic relationship; its historical mechanism remains unresolved.

schemaObservations.reason: Alice Mary (Ross) Colver is a documented personal-name form, while Mary Randall is a relationship claim whose mechanism is unresolved. Both would be damaged by one generic aliases column.
schemaObservations.designPressure: Model creator name claims separately from source-circle/pseudonym/house-name relationships.

schemaObservations.reason: Babs at Home has a 1921 copyright claim and a 1924 LOC digitized manifestation. A single work.publication_date would silently erase the edition distinction.
schemaObservations.designPressure: Attestation-level date claims and edition-level dates must precede any governed work-level first-publication field.

schemaObservations.reason: The same copyright, archive, or catalog source supports creator identity, title identity, dates, contributor roles, and rights questions.
schemaObservations.designPressure: Do not bury evidence as duplicated JSON arrays on every table; use reusable evidence sources/assertions or equivalent relations.

schemaObservations.reason: Adventures on a Hilltop versus Adventure on a Hilltop and the two Heart title strings require clusters that can remain unresolved and later split or merge.
schemaObservations.designPressure: Do not implement work identity as a mutable foreign key on title_attestation alone.

schemaObservations.reason: Mud Wumps is catalogued as series member four even though a witness has never been seen. Series membership and work/witness existence are separate claims.
schemaObservations.designPressure: Series membership needs status, order confidence, and evidence rather than a simple series_id column on work.

schemaObservations.reason: A title may be witnessed, digitized, public-domain, partially recovered, or currently republished in different combinations.
schemaObservations.designPressure: Avoid one overloaded work.status enum for identity, witness, rights, digital availability, and recovery state.

schemaObservations.reason: Image Cascade's current Joan Foster editions are strong evidence that Write Now should treat the series as rights-sensitive, but they do not by themselves establish the complete legal chain.
schemaObservations.designPressure: Model current manifestation/publisher evidence separately from governed rights determinations.

schemaObservations.reason: The architecture must later support attributed, collective, anonymous, translated, and disputed creator relationships without changing work identity.
schemaObservations.designPressure: Historical Work should not own a simplistic creators array as the final relational model; authorship claims should be first-class.

schemaObservations.reason: The Dodd archive is substantial but begins in 1929 and omits many early works; modern aggregators are noisy. A count without a coverage ledger would create false completeness.
schemaObservations.designPressure: Corpus completeness must be derived from documented source-family coverage, not title count alone.

schemaObservations.reason: Mud Wumps matters to recovery of the Wish Fairy corpus even though it cannot enter normal reconstruction without a witness.
schemaObservations.designPressure: The data model must retain witnessed, unwitnessed, and possibly unpublished corpus members without forcing every title into a production queue.
